Here is a small experiment you can try at any front desk in the world. Walk up and say, where is the elevator? You will get an answer, but you will probably not get a smile. Now try it again, and this time start with, could you tell me where the elevator is? The information is exactly the same, and so is the person behind the desk. But the second question gives them a moment, and it tells them you see a person and not a machine. Notice one more thing. In the second version the verb moves to the end. Where the elevator is, not where is the elevator. That small change is the most common mistake people make, and it is very easy to hear. So once you fix it, people notice.

Good afternoon, and welcome to Miami International Airport. If you are wondering where to find a taxi, taxis and ride shares are on the lower level, outside door number six. Passengers who need to find out about connecting flights should go to the information desk in the center of the main hall, which is open twenty-four hours a day. Please note that the moving walkway near gate D twelve is out of order this afternoon, so allow ten extra minutes to reach your gate. Complimentary Wi-Fi is available everywhere in the terminal. And if you are not sure whether your flight is on time, please check the screens or ask any member of our staff.
